steps.body: 37 + 25: the ones make 12 — too many! Trade ten ones for a rod: 6 tens 2 ones, 62.
steps.narration: Thirty-seven plus twenty-five: the ones make twelve — too many! Trade ten ones for a rod: six tens two ones, sixty-two.

widget.prompt: 37 + 25 makes 5 tens and 12 ones. Trade ten ones for a rod and build 62 in standard form.

commonBuilds.feedback: That's 62's untraded pile — 5 tens 12 ones. Now TRADE ten ones for one rod: 6 tens 2 ones.
That builds 72 — you added the new rod but kept all 12 ones. Trading REMOVES ten ones: 6 tens 2 ones.

widget.missFeedback: 12 ones = 1 rod + 2 ones. So 5+1 = 6 tens, 2 ones.
widget.successFeedback: Ten ones became a rod — 6 tens 2 ones is 62!

predict.prompt: 37 + 25 piles up as 5 tens and 12 ones. Is that already 62?

options.label: In value, yes — but the ones overflow, so trade ten of them

predict.reveal: 5 tens + 12 ones is WORTH 62 — the amount is right, the form isn't. Ten of those ones bundle into a sixth rod: 6 tens, 2 ones. Trading changes the look, never the value.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents regroup add.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for regroup add must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines regroup add.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

commonErrors.feedback: The traded ten got dropped! Ones 7+5=12 carries one ten: 62, not 52.
That wrote the 12 next to the 5 tens. Trade ten of the 12: 6 tens 2 ones = 62.

steps.body: The traded rod joins the tens. Never drop it, never keep the ten loose ones.
steps.narration: The traded rod joins the tens. Never drop it, never keep the ten loose ones.

widget.prompt: Match each sum to whether its ones need a trade.

pairErrors.feedback: 43 + 25 has ones 3+5=8 — under ten, so it's the safe one.

widget.missFeedback: Add just the ones digits: 8+6=14, 3+5=8, 9+7=16. Ten or more → trade.
widget.successFeedback: You can spot a trade before it happens!

widget.prompt: The ones in 48 + 36 make 14. Trade 10 ones for a ten, then enter the standard-form total.

commonErrors.feedback: The traded ten got dropped! Ones 8+6=14 carries one ten: 84, not 74.
That wrote 14 next to the 7 tens. Trade ten of the 14: 8 tens 4 ones = 84.

explanationVariants: A trade happens when the ones reach ten or more — like 7+5=12.
Ten-or-more ones can't fit one digit, so ten of them become a rod.

widget.prompt: When do the ones need a trade?

options.label: when they make 10 or more
options.feedback: Yes — ten ones become one rod; only the leftovers stay as ones.

options.label: when they make exactly 9
options.feedback: 9 ones still fit in one digit — a trade starts at TEN.

options.label: every single time
options.feedback: Sums like 43 + 25 (ones 3+5=8) need no trade — only ten-or-more does.

widget.prompt: A learner writes 316 for 29 + 17 by placing 16 ones beside 3 tens. Trade the ones and enter the corrected total.

commonErrors.feedback: The traded ten got dropped! Ones 9+7=16 carries one ten: 46, not 36.
That wrote 16 next to the 3 tens. Trade ten of the 16: 4 tens 6 ones = 46.

takeaways: Ones at 10+ trade ten for a rod.
The traded rod joins the tens.
Check the ones first to spot a trade.
steps.teaser: next chapter: subtracting — sometimes a rod breaks back into ones!

concept.body: Slow it down. 15 + 17: ones 5+7=12. Ten of them become a rod. Tens 1+1+1=3, ones 2: 32.
concept.narration: Fifteen plus seventeen: ones five plus seven is twelve. Ten of them become a rod. Tens one plus one plus one is three, ones two: thirty-two.

commonErrors.feedback: The traded ten got dropped! Ones 5+7=12 carries one ten: 32.
That wrote 12 next to the 2 tens. Trade: 3 tens 2 ones = 32.
